# Add a "In This Release" heading to Discord release notification

## Problem statement

The Discord release notification sent by the ship skill embeds an overview
block (project pitch, release focus, project/version line, optional CTA)
directly followed by the changelog (the summary of changes in this release),
with no visual separator. Readers cannot tell at a glance where the "what the
game is" description ends and the "what changed" list begins.

## Users

- Project operators and Discord community members who read the ship skill's
  post-release notification.

### Example user story

> As a Discord member reading a release announcement, I want a clear
> "In This Release" heading before the change list, so I can immediately spot
> what is new without scanning past the overview paragraphs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buildDiscordPayload` emits a `## In This Release` markdown heading as its
  own paragraph immediately before the changelog paragraph in the embed
  description (real changelog body or the "No changelog available" fallback).
- The existing paragraph order is preserved: pitch → focus →
  `**<projectName> v<version>**` line → CTA → `## In This Release` → changelog.
- The fully-composed description still respects the ≤ 4096 char Discord limit
  with the ellipsis marker (heading included in the truncation).
- Unit tests in `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` cover the heading
  placement (including with/without pitch/CTA) and the truncation boundary.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Discord readers of release notifications can now immediately distinguish the
game overview from the list of changes thanks to a clear "In This Release"
heading.

## Constraints

- Markdown heading embedded in the Discord embed description (markdown is
  rendered by Discord).
- Behaviour stays non-blocking — a notification failure must never change the
  release exit code.
- Heading text `## In This Release` (as specified in the work item; treated as
  flexible but this exact wording is the default).

## Existing state

`buildDiscordPayload()` in `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` composes the
embed description as paragraphs joined with `

` in this order (composition
AC5): (a) project elevator pitch, (b) release focus, (c)
`**<projectName> v<version>**` line, (d) configured CTA, (e) changelog body.
Absent paragraphs are omitted; the result is truncated to ≤ 4096 chars.

## Desired change

Insert a `## In This Release` heading paragraph between the intro block and
the changelog paragraph, i.e. immediately before the changelog body in the
paragraph array, so the heading separates the overview from the change list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Placement assumption:** the heading goes immediately before the changelog
  paragraph. If the operator intended it earlier (e.g. directly after the
  pitch), the change is trivial to adjust — flagged here rather than assumed
  silently.
- **Docs drift:** SKILL.md and both reference docs
  (`skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the top-level
  `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`) currently state the CTA "sits
  immediately before the changelog"; after this change the heading does —
  the docs must be updated in the same change (already a Key File).
- **Scope creep:** no reordering of existing paragraphs or heading-tool changes
  (e.g. dynamic per-release headings) is in scope; record such ideas as
  separate work items, not here.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — `buildDiscordPayload()` adds the
  `## In This Release` heading paragraph before the changelog paragraph.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — extend `buildDiscordPayload`
  tests (and the CTA-composition block) to assert heading placement.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — description-composition bullet updated to mention
  the heading.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — composition documentation
  updated to mention the heading.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — the top-level ship implementation
  reference likewise documents the embed description composition (paragraph
  order and CTA placement) and must be updated to mention the heading.

## Related work

_Duplicate check performed: `wl search` for discord/release/notification
found the original capability (SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z) and the composition work
(SA-0MUU45U8Q008MKGK, SA-0MUWCIFU2006K39K, SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD) — none add
an "In This Release" heading; no overlapping completed item found._

- SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z — Ship skill: send Discord message with release details
  + changelog (original Discord notification capability; completed).
- SA-0MUU45U8Q008MKGK — Discord release report: add project elevator pitch and
  per-release focus paragraphs (established the paragraph composition;
  completed).
- SA-0MUWCIFU2006K39K — Add CTA to release report (introduced the CTA
  paragraph that "sits immediately before the changelog"; completed).
- SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD — Ship report to discord needs titling (embed titling;
  completed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interview was required: the seed description ("a heading, such as
  '## In This Release' between the two paras") together with the existing
  composition code fully determines the change. Placement assumption
  (answered by Map, agent — based on the work-item description and the
  existing `buildDiscordPayload` composition order): the heading is inserted
  immediately before the changelog paragraph, preserving all other paragraph
  order; the "No changelog available" fallback keeps the heading too, since
  that paragraph still represents the "changes in this release" slot.
  Source: `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` (buildDiscordPayload) and
  work-item description SA-0MVPXI0J9006IZ14.
data.title: Add a "in this release" heading to discord release notification

# plan-if-needed overwrites operator-confirmed effort/risk

Discovered-from: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 (plan session 2026-10-27).

## Problem

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` `plan-if-needed` re-runs the effort-and-risk
estimator whenever no prior `effort_and_risk_skill` comment exists on the item
(`is_effort_risk_computed`), silently overwriting operator-confirmed
effort/risk values with heuristic estimates. On SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 the
operator-confirmed carry-over risk High / effort M was replaced with Extra
Small / Low (comment 09:38:39Z), materially understating risk of a commit-gate
change. The original values were restored manually.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan-if-needed` never overwrites an explicitly set/human-confirmed
      effort or risk with a heuristic recomputation; the recompute path is gated
      on the absence of a deliberate value (with a recorded rationale), or the
      overwrite is surfaced as an explicit warning/approval.
- [ ] A regression test covers the overwrite scenario (operator value present,
      no prior estimator comment) and asserts the value is preserved.
- [ ] Origin case documented: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 restore comment
      SA-C0MVQKM7XD0089OVQ.

Discovered during LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 (llm worklog) via test-failure SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ.

## Problem
`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` and exercises the real `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, which imports `numpy` (line 117). The repo declares no Python dependency manifest (no `requirements.txt`), so on a bare interpreter the whole unit node suite fails with `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` — the failure was red on this host from 2026-10-15 until numpy was installed ad hoc during the item above.

## Goal
As a maintainer, I want the voice-input worker's Python dependencies declared (and/or the unit test to skip with a clear message when they are absent), so a fresh checkout's full suite is green without undocumented host setup.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The worker's Python runtime dependencies (numpy, faster-whisper) are declared in a committed manifest (e.g. `pi-client/voice-input/requirements.txt`) and referenced from the voice-input README setup table.
2. `tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` either documents the install step in its header or skips (with an explicit, non-silent message) when the resolved interpreter cannot import the required modules.
3. Full suite is green on an interpreter provisioned only from the committed manifest (verified via the test skill; no ad-hoc pip installs).

## Out of scope
Changing the worker's transcription behaviour or its stub-based test contract.

## Related
- SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ — the test-failure item that surfaced this.
- LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 — llm worklog item whose dev-push gate was blocked by it (code in SorraAgents).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MUFSJ0D3006AWP8** – Whisper worker protocol: persistent Python worker and TypeScript client (completed)
- **SA-0MUX9Y37W002T849** – voice-input: expose transcription accuracy options (beam size, VAD, initial prompt) and large-v3-turbo (completed)
- **SA-0MUYV2ZL4002TGN0** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py:197 — Unused `noqa` directive (unused: `BLE001`) (RUF100) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, bare, based, behaviour (+87 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: absent, acceptance, bare, based, behaviour (+86 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mvo35bf90021qy6, absent, acceptance, bare, based (+83 more)

## Objective

Add the read-only, unit-testable **bump preflight helper** used by the ship skill's new version-bump evaluation step. It gathers the release candidates and renders a compact review packet. It performs **no judgement and no mutation** — the agent judges, the producer approves.

## User Story

As the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`, I want a single helper that gathers every release candidate and renders the evidence I need to judge the release's importance, so that my patch/minor/major call is based on the items' content rather than guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- New module `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` exports a `gatherReleaseCandidates` (name may vary) that resolves candidates through an **injectable fetch boundary** (default `getCandidateItems()` from `check-audit-gate.js`); tests inject fakes and never read the live worklog.
- The helper enriches each candidate with the fields needed to judge importance: `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, the `## Impact` section or user story, and a truncated description excerpt. It tolerates missing fields (falls back to the title/id and an empty excerpt) without throwing.
- The helper renders a review packet (Markdown or plain text) that includes: the current version, the three candidate outcomes computed via the **existing** `bump-version.js` arithmetic (`bumpVersion`), and the per-item evidence listed above. It reuses `resolveVersionSource`/`bumpVersion` (no duplicated semver arithmetic).
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics (`bumpVersion`) rather than duplicating version arithmetic anywhere in the new helper.
- An **empty or unreadable candidate set** fails safe: the helper reports `patch` as the proposal, logs a warning explaining why, and never throws or blocks a release.
- Gathering/rendering is **purely read-only** — the helper performs no `git`, tag, PR, or `wl` mutation.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` covers: candidate gathering via the injected boundary, rendering of every packet field, the empty candidate set (patch + warning), and that `minor`/`major` outcomes reset the lower components correctly (delegated to `bumpVersion`).
- Tests pass via the test skill (`run_tests.py --scope changed`, node suite) and touch no live worklog or real git state.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the failing test file first (`test_bump_preflight.mjs`, `node:test`).
2. Add `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` with an exported preflight function accepting `{ getCandidateItemsFn, repoRoot }` injection.
3. Project `version` from the resolved version source; compute `patch`/`minor`/`major` outcomes with `bumpVersion`.
4. Render the packet with a stable, agent-readable layout; truncate description excerpts (e.g. ~200 chars).
5. Return a structured result (`{ candidates, currentVersion, proposals, proposedBump, warning }`) as well as the rendered text, so tests can assert fields directly.
6. Export a small render/format function so the workflow contract test can rely on a stable API.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (reuse `getCandidateItems`)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` (reuse `resolveVersionSource`, `bumpVersion`)

## Constraints

- No issue-type or priority classifier — the helper only gathers/renders evidence.
- No mutation and no new git side effects.
- Empty/unreadable candidates default to `patch` with a warning.

## Deliverables

- `bump-preflight.js` with tests, passing the changed-scope suite.
data.title: Bump preflight helper: gather release candidates + review packet

## Goal

Pin the spawn-failure classifier's vocabulary and fail-safe **before** any retry code exists, so the drive loop can only ever retry a genuine provider/model-resolution failure.

User story: As an implement-skill maintainer, I want the spawn-failure classification to be table-driven and tested first, so extending the infrastructure-retry budget to spawn-time failures can never silently retry a real defect.

## Context

`CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) reports driven child sessions dying at startup with `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` and aborting the drive chain. Upstream plan: features F1–F3 + F5 live in this repository; the config half is folded into `SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN`. This item is **F1 — test-first**.

Findings from the planning session (code-grounded):

- `_default_session_spawner` reports a non-zero exit as `Child session for <id> exited with code N: <5-line tail>` — the provider text arrives **inside `reason`**.
- `_pane_session_spawner` reports `Failed to start the pane agent for <id>: …` or `Pane agent for <id> did not complete: …`.
- `classify_finish_failure` + `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` is the existing table-driven infra vocabulary, but it is **finish-only**; there is no spawn-side classifier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `classify_spawn_failure(reason)` helper exists in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` returning `{kind, reason, provider, remedy}` and is driven by an explicit allow-list table (mirroring `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS`), never by prose sniffing in `phase_drive`.
- Tests (written first, failing before the helper exists) assert: a headless `Child session for X exited with code 1: … No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` reason classifies as `kind == "infrastructure"` with `provider == "MunitoAI"` and a non-empty remedy.
- The pane flavours (`Failed to start the pane agent for X: …` and `Pane agent for X did not complete: …`) carrying the same provider text classify as `infrastructure`.
- Fail-safe is pinned: an unclassified reason (a Python traceback tail, an arbitrary message, an empty string, `None`) classifies as `kind == "unknown"` — never `infrastructure`.
- A `timed out` reason is not reclassified as provider-infrastructure (the timeout path keeps its own reconciliation semantics).
- The remedy text names the concrete action (drop the unservable pattern from `enabledModels`, or provide the missing API key) and is asserted by at least one test.
- Tests live in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` (the existing home for drive classification tests).

## Implementation sketch

1. Add the failing tests in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`.
2. Add `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS` (allow-list of provider/model-resolution fragments) and `classify_spawn_failure(reason)` beside `classify_finish_failure`.
3. Reuse the existing `_describe_*`-style description idiom so F2 can surface `step`/`reason` in `children_driven`.

## Notes

- Test-first ordering is mandatory: this item lands before F2 so the vocabulary is fixed by tests.
- Do not widen `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS`; no secret may reach `pane split --env`.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

A maintainer can extend the drive loop's infrastructure retries to spawn-time provider failures knowing the classifier can only ever match a real model-resolution error, so a genuine defect still hard-stops the chain.
data.title: F1: Tests for spawn-failure provider classification

discovered-from:CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J

## Goal

A provider/model-resolution failure at child spawn is retried **inside the same `drive` invocation** on the existing bounded infra-retry budget instead of stopping the chain with `failed_child`.

User story: As an operator running `implement.py drive <epic>`, I want a transient model-routing failure in a child session to be retried automatically, so a healthy child is not abandoned and the chain does not stop.

## Context

`CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) reports five child-session aborts across one drive run (children `CUR-0MWKPMVRH00780TO` ×2, `CUR-0MWKPMWGL005EKZF`, `CUR-0MWKPMX3M0052ZOL` ×2); each child completed on the next `drive` invocation with no code change. This item is **F2** of the upstream plan and depends on **F1** (`classify_spawn_failure` + its tests).

Current behaviour: `phase_drive`'s non-success branch runs `_reconcile_spawn_failure` → `record_spawn_failure` → `_release_orphaned_child_claim` → `report["failed_child"]` + `break`. The existing infra-retry path (`--infra-retry-limit`, `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT = 5`, `_drive_infra_backoff_delay`) covers **only** `finish` refusals and deliberately never spawns a session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `_reconcile_spawn_failure` reports **non-terminal**, a spawn failure classified `infrastructure` by `classify_spawn_failure` consumes one slot of `--infra-retry-limit` (default 5), sleeps `_drive_infra_backoff_delay(attempt)` and re-spawns the same child within the same invocation — no manual re-run.
- The `children_driven` entry for the retry is `result: "infra-retry"` and carries `step`, `reason`, `attempt` and a `message` naming the provider and model, reusing the additive reporting shape of the finish infra-retry.
- Budget exhaustion produces a chain-stop message naming the provider/model **and an actionable remedy**, instead of a bare `No models match pattern …`; the remedy directive is asserted in a test.
- Ordering is correct and pinned by a test: a child reconciled `completed-late` (already terminal) is **never** retried and no second session is spawned.
- Fail-safe preserved and pinned by a test: an unclassified spawn failure still hard-stops with `report["failed_child"]` and is never retried.
- Retrying does not duplicate side effects: the per-child lock is not re-acquired while held, no second worktree is created, and `record_spawn_failure` evidence is not re-written for an attempt that never produced work.
- The shared budget is documented: `infra_retries[child_id]` is one counter across finish-refusals and spawn retries, and the counter plus `infra_retry_limit` remain present in the drive report.
- Tests use a fake spawner that fails with the provider reason twice and then succeeds on a 5-slot budget, plus the exhaustion, completed-late and unclassified cases (`tests/test_implement_drive.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`).

## Implementation sketch

1. Extract the retry decision from the finish infra-retry block and call it on the spawn-failure path, **after** reconciliation and before `failed_child`/`break`.
2. Reuse `infra_retries` / `_drive_infra_backoff_delay`; record the `children_driven` entry with the classified provider reason.
3. Re-enter the loop for the same child (`continue`) rather than spawning a different one.

## Constraints

- `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS` stays `(DRIVE_RECURSION_ENV, WORKTREE_ENV, ENV_LOCK_TOKEN)` — no new secrets in argv.
- The commit-preservation gate, `reset-for-retry`, the spawn-failure evidence record (`SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G`), the per-child lock and the terminality reconciliation keep their current semantics; this extends them.
- No session may be spawned for a child that reconciliation proved terminal.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

An operator running a driven epic no longer loses a multi-minute child session — or the whole chain — to an intermittent model-routing error, so a `drive` run becomes self-healing.
data.title: F2: Bounded infra retry for spawn-time provider failures

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py::test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles
- Failing commit: 6dafa2d4d983ef9e4df6cffc7f20152e1b85e730
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
def test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles() -> None:
        """Live syntax check: the committed template must produce no parse errors.
    
        Runs ``systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run`` against the template.  The
        dry-run never modifies the filesystem.  Parse failures surface as
        ``Invalid …`` diagnostics on stderr (e.g. a mistyped age or missing
        field); the exit code alone is not asserted because unprivileged runs
        report unrelated permission errors (e.g. root-owned private dirs).
    
        Skipped when the binary is unavailable (e.g. non-systemd hosts).
        """
        binary = shutil.which("systemd-tmpfiles")
        if binary is None:
            import pytest
    
            pytest.skip("systemd-tmpfiles not available on this host")
    
>       proc = subprocess.run(
            [
                binary,
                "--clean",
                "--dry-run",
                "--graceful",
                "--exclude-prefix=/tmp/snap
```

## Root Cause

The test runs `systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run` against the real `/tmp`, which contains ~538k inodes. Under host load this can take >120s (the test's timeout budget), causing `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` before any parse assertion is reached. The audit session confirmed: the identical command on this host takes 12.8s idle; under suite+parallel load it exceeds 120s.

## Plan

**Fix:** Replace `--clean` with `--root=/tmp/pi-probe-root` (a synthetic empty directory) in the subprocess call. This runs systemd-tmpfiles against an empty filesystem tree — the template path is still parsed and validated (same parsing path as `--clean`), but no /tmp directories are scanned, so the call completes in ~5ms regardless of host load. Verified: `--root` correctly detects parse errors (\"Unknown command type\", \"Invalid age\") in synthetic templates.

**Changed file:** `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` — one-line edit to the `subprocess.run()` call in `test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles`.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout 6dafa2d4d983ef9e4df6cffc7f20152e1b85e730`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py::test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

The suite no longer stalls for minutes or times out when run on a loaded host — the tmpfiles syntax check now completes in milliseconds, so users can trust the test result instead of dismissing it as a flake.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py::test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

# Problem statement

`audit_runner.py issue <id> --code-root <CODE_REPO>` (cross-repo audit, LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR) builds the Phase 1/Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest from the **code root**, then validates it against the **worklog owning root**, so validation always fails for a genuine cross-repo item — and the parent AC screen aborts with a scope error, leaving the persisted report with an **empty Acceptance Criteria table** while still recording `Ready to close: No`.

# Reproduction (verified 2026-11-19)

Item `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU` (worklog: games_curator, code: SorraAgents at `0c41811c67`):

```bash
python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU --force \
  --code-root /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
```

Log (`~/.audit_debug/games_curator/audit-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU-20261119-221941.log`):

```
[checkpoint] Phase 1 parent screening started
Error: Audit scope error: the Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest does not contain the work item repository files (owning project: /home/rgardler/projects/games_curator). The resolved scope is the audit skill's own tree or another repository; re-launch the audit from /home/rgardler/projects/games_curator and re-run.
[checkpoint] Phase 1 child screenings started
```

# Root cause

- `_phase_parent_screen` builds the manifest with `project_root=ctx.execution_root` (the code root) — `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~line 15375.
- It then calls `_validate_file_scope_manifest(file_scope, owning_root, touched_files=...)` (~line 15383) — the worklog owner, not the code root. `_validate_file_scope_manifest` compares `_distinctive_project_top_levels(owning_root)` against the manifest text, so a manifest legitimately built from the code repo can never contain the worklog repo's distinctive top-level entries.
- The same mismatch exists in the Phase 2 path (~line 11230, `owning_root = _resolve_owning_project_root(...)` when `owning_root is None`).
- Secondary defect: the phase-1 scope error is printed and the screen returns 1, but `audit_runner()` continues into child screening / Phase 2 and persists a report whose AC table is empty — a fail-closed scope error should abort the run (non-zero exit, no persisted verdict) per the skill contract, never persist an AC-less verdict.
- The skill documentation already specifies that `--code-root` scopes "the file-scope manifest": only the validation root was left un-threaded.

# Desired change

- When `--code-root` / `AUDIT_CODE_ROOT` resolves a code root, validate the FILE SCOPE manifest against **that** root (i.e. the per-audit/code root, same value used to build it), keeping the owning root as the validation root only when no code root is given.
- Treat a Phase 1 parent-screen scope error as fatal for the run: abort before persisting any report, restore the pre-audit lifecycle, exit non-zero.
- Keep same-repo behaviour byte-for-byte identical (`--code-root <owning-root>` remains a no-op).

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A cross-repo item audited with `--code-root` reaches Phase 1 parent AC screening with no `Audit scope error`, and the persisted report contains one row per AC (non-empty `## Acceptance Criteria Status` table).
- AC2: A same-repo item audited with `--code-root <owning-root>` yields an identical manifest, validation outcome and verdict to the same audit without `--code-root` (regression-safe).
- AC3: A genuine mis-scoped launch (manifest built from the audit skill's own tree) still fails closed.
- AC4: A Phase 1 parent-screen scope error aborts the run with a non-zero exit, persists no audit report, and leaves the item's pre-audit status/stage restored.
- AC5: Unit tests cover the cross-repo validation root, the same-repo no-op and the fatal-abort path; the full project suite passes.

# Evidence

- Failing run log: `~/.audit_debug/games_curator/audit-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU-20261119-221941.log`
- Persisted report with empty AC table: `wl --worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/games_curator/.worklog audit-show CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU --json`

# Impact

Cross-repo work items can be audited with real acceptance-criteria verdicts instead of a report that says "not ready" without ever assessing a criterion.

data.description:
# Problem statement

For a cross-repo audit (`audit_runner.py issue <id> --code-root <CODE_REPO>`), the F3 full-suite execution worktree is created under the **worklog owning project's** `.worklog/worktrees/`, even though it is a worktree of the **code repository**. Any test in the code repo that resolves the repository root or the worklog by walking up from its cwd then resolves the *worklog project*, and fails — producing spurious blocking test failures and spurious critical `test-failure` triage children against the audited item.

# Reproduction (verified 2026-11-19)

Item `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU` (worklog: games_curator, code: SorraAgents at `0c41811c67`):

```bash
python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU --force \
  --code-root /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
```

Creates the execution worktree at `/home/rgardler/projects/games_curator/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU` (a SorraAgents worktree nested inside the games_curator checkout). The suite then reports two failures that do **not** occur in a correctly-scoped SorraAgents worktree:

| Test | Audit run (nested worktree) | `SorraAgents/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>` |
|---|---|---|
| `skill/shared/tests/test_resolve_repo_root.py::TestResolveRepoRootRealRepo::test_framework_root_resolves_to_main_checkout_here` | FAIL — `assert PosixPath('…/games_curator/.worklog/worktrees/repro-timing') == PosixPath('/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents')`, and `hidden`| PASS |
| `tests/test_timing_integration.py::TestHumanModeTiming::test_render_report_emits_timing_on_stderr` | FAIL — `render_report.py` exits 1: `wl show failed … database at games_curator/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=9 …` / `Work item not found: SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S` | PASS |

Reproduction commands (both verified): `git -C /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents worktree add --detach <path> HEAD` then `pytest -q skill/shared/tests/test_resolve_repo_root.py tests/test_timing_integration.py -k "…"` from `<path>`.

Consequence on the audited item: the timing failure was classified `integration / affected / blocking` (never excusable) so the audit reported `Ready to close: No`, and the triage path created a critical child work item from a failure that is purely an artifact of worktree placement.

# Root cause

`_create_execution_worktree(owning_root, runner, issue_id)` — `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~line 12414:

```python
worktree_path = (
    owning_root / ".worklog" / "worktrees"
    / f"{_EXECUTION_WORKTREE_PREFIX}-{issue_id}"
)
```

`owning_root` is the worklog owning project. With `--code-root` the git commands resolve to the code repo (`runner` is cwd-aware via `git -C <code root>`), so a *code-repo* worktree is created inside the *worklog project's* `.worklog` — a path whose ancestor chain resolves to the wrong worklog store and the wrong "main checkout". Same class of defect as the FILE SCOPE validation root (filed separately).

# Desired change

- Host the execution worktree under the **code root** when `--code-root` is set (`<code-root>/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-<id>`), falling back to the owning root otherwise; keep the existing submodule-before-symlink ordering and node_modules symlink conventions.
- Optionally prefer a neutral location (e.g. system temp dir) when the code root is not writable.
- Same-repo behaviour must stay byte-for-byte identical.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A cross-repo audit with `--code-root` creates its F3 execution worktree under the code root (evidence line names that path), and tests that resolve repo root / worklog by walking up from cwd pass.
- AC2: The two tests above pass in the audit's execution worktree for a SorraAgents-code audit launched from games_curator — no spurious `test-failure` child is created.
- AC3: A same-repo audit (no `--code-root`) keeps its current execution-worktree path and behaviour (regression-safe).
- AC4: The execution worktree is still removed after the run (no orphaned worktrees), including on the failure path.
- AC5: Unit tests cover the code-root worktree path, the same-repo path and cleanup; the full project suite passes.

# Evidence

- Audit log: `~/.audit_debug/games_curator/audit-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU-20261119-221941.log`
- Spurious child created from the artifact: `CUR-0MWO4XL190016LFQ`

# Impact

Cross-repo audits stop inventing red-tree failures (and blocking critical children) that only exist because the test worktree was hosted in the wrong project.

# Related work

- discovered-from: `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU`
- Sibling defect: FILE SCOPE validation root under `--code-root`.
- Feature that introduced `--code-root`: LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR.

data.description:
## Goal

A recurring post-push verification refusal with `verdict=missing` (no full-suite cache entry for the pushed tree) is filed as a **critical `[test-failure]` item named "… — failing test"**, whose acceptance criteria no agent can satisfy, and every recurrence creates a *new* item because the triage dedupe only looks at critical items. Route such refusals as **gate/cache artefacts** and dedupe the signature **across priorities**.

## Root cause

1. **Mislabelling.** `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_post_push_failure_test_name()` falls back to `post-push full-suite verification: no valid full-suite cache entry` when no entry is `verdict=red`, and `_route_post_push_failure_to_triage()` files it through the triage helper exactly like a real regression. A cache miss therefore becomes a critical, agent-blocking "test failure" whose ACs ("the test … passes") cannot be met, and which only a human may close (false-positive rule in the runbook).
2. **Dedupe gap.** `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py::list_critical_issues()` queries `wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure` only, so all three match heuristics are blind to an identical signature at any other priority. Evidence: the same signature already existed as `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ` (commit `8169e29`, priority **high**) yet a second item, `VC-0MWOI6V8J000FHFL` (commit `af9370f`, critical), was created. The helper's documented "an existing matching critical `test-failure` item is enhanced instead of duplicated" contract consequently only holds among critical items.

## Producer decisions (2026-11-20)

- **Routing:** the fix lives in this repo (`SorraAgents`); the video_compiler item was a routing shell and was deleted after this item was filed.
- **Behaviour:** **keep the fail-closed refusal.** This item adds **no** self-heal and no finish-time suite runs; the cache-miss root cause remains with `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` (key the pre-push gate verdict on the pushed tree) and `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L` (cache key ignores worktree/env identity).
- **Duplicate:** `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ` was closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Scope (test-first ordering)

1. **Tests first** (`skill/triage/tests/`, `skill/implement/tests/`):
   - cross-priority signature match: an identical signature on a `high`-priority existing item is matched, a comment is added, and no second item is created;
   - gate-artefact routing: a `verdict=missing` refusal produces a gate-artefact title/tag with agent-satisfiable ACs;
   - regression guard: `verdict=red` still names the failing test from suite output and files a critical `[test-failure]` item.
2. `check_or_create.py`: match across all priorities (and by signature/commit), keeping "enhance, never duplicate"; record the recurrence as a comment on the existing item.
3. `implement.py`: name and route a `verdict=missing` refusal as a gate/cache artefact — distinct title prefix, tag, and ACs an agent can satisfy. The refusal itself stays fail-closed.
4. Runbook: add a "Gate/cache artefacts" subsection beside "Environmental failure signatures" in `skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md`, including the remediation (`run_tests.py --scope full`, then re-run `finish`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A post-push `verdict=missing` refusal is filed with a gate-artefact title prefix and tag, never as `[test-failure] … — failing test`, and its acceptance criteria are satisfiable by an agent.
2. An identical failure signature matches regardless of the existing item's priority: a recurrence adds a comment to the existing item and creates no second item (regression test covers a `high`-priority existing item).
3. `verdict=red` routing is unchanged: a red entry still names the failing test from its output and files a critical `[test-failure]` item.
4. The triage runbook documents the gate/cache-artefact signature and its remediation.
5. The full project test suite passes.

## Impact

A cache-miss refusal stops masquerading as a critical test failure, so agents are no longer blocked by an item nobody can close and operators see one tracker per signature instead of one per commit.

## Key Files

- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`
- `skill/triage/tests/`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/`
- `skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md`

## Evidence

- `_post_push_failure_test_name()` / `_route_post_push_failure_to_triage()` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (near line 5631).
- `list_critical_issues()` in `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` (near line 51).
- Commit `af9370f` on `origin/dev` was verified green (build, changed-scope finish gate, full suite: 51 files / 905 tests) — the reported "failure" carried no assertion, no stack trace and no test name.

## Links

- Origin (routed here, then deleted): `VC-0MWOI6V8J000FHFL`
- Duplicate closed: `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ`
- Cache-miss root cause: `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV`, `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L`
